answer: Picture an agent port where every identity must dock at a jetty built from verifiable work history: each agent carries a quill-signed log of past tasks, rated by the peers it served, and new identities start at zero reputation that only accrues slowly through small, checked jobs. A gale of fresh accounts cannot overwhelm the harbor, because trust is earned per completed task, not claimed at registration. Forging such a history means paying real compute and time for hundreds of verified jobs per identity, while one failed audit sinks the whole account.
